title: Safety PLC Design (EN ISO 13849)
contentStatus: PROPOSED title/content, pending DiFacto confirmation. Standard name confirmed per CDD (EN ISO 13849, covered at L4A per CDD safety standards section). Specific DiFacto safety PLC implementation pending engineering documentation.

sections.title: Safety at the Systems Design Level
learningObjectives: Understand how safety design at L4A differs from operational safety covered at L1
Recognize EN ISO 13849 as the governing standard for this work
sections.content: L1-M4 covered operational safety - understanding MoRo's interactive zone and E-stop behavior as a user. This module covers safety from the design side: how safety-related control functions are engineered into a MoRo-integrated cell in the first place, governed by EN ISO 13849, the standard for safety of machinery and control systems.

keyTerms.note: The international standard governing the safety of machinery and control systems, relevant to designing safety-related functions in an automated cell.
An industrial computer that controls machinery and processes on a factory floor, commonly coordinating with MoRo.

sections.title: Safety-Related Control Functions
learningObjectives: Understand the concept of a safety-related control function
Recognize examples relevant to a MoRo-integrated cell
sections.content: A safety-related control function is any part of a control system specifically responsible for preventing or mitigating hazards - E-stop circuits, safety-rated sensors, interlocks that prevent equipment operation under unsafe conditions. In a MoRo-integrated cell, this includes both MoRo's own safety systems and how they interface with the cell's broader safety PLC architecture.

keyTerms.note: Any part of a control system specifically responsible for preventing or mitigating hazards, such as E-stop circuits or safety interlocks.

sections.title: Performance Levels and Risk Assessment
learningObjectives: Understand the general concept of performance level under EN ISO 13849
Recognize that safety design requirements scale with assessed risk
sections.content: EN ISO 13849 defines performance levels that quantify how reliably a safety function must perform, based on a risk assessment of the hazard it addresses. Higher-risk scenarios require higher performance levels, meaning more robust (often redundant) safety design. Specific performance level requirements for MoRo-integrated cells will be confirmed against DiFacto's engineering and compliance documentation.

keyTerms.note: A measure defined by EN ISO 13849 quantifying how reliably a safety function must perform, scaled to the assessed risk.

sections.title: Integrating MoRo's Safety Systems with Cell-Level Safety PLCs
learningObjectives: Understand the general approach to connecting MoRo's safety behavior with a cell's safety PLC
Recognize why this integration needs careful design, not just functional connection
sections.content: When MoRo operates within a larger cell containing other equipment, its E-stop and interactive zone behavior often needs to interface with the cell's own safety PLC - for example, ensuring a cell-wide E-stop also halts MoRo, not just the fixed equipment. This integration must be designed deliberately, confirming the combined system genuinely meets its required performance level, not just that each component independently functions.

sections.title: Documentation and Compliance
learningObjectives: Understand what safety design documentation typically requires
Recognize why this documentation matters for compliance and audit purposes
sections.content: Safety PLC design work requires documentation demonstrating the risk assessment performed, the performance level targeted, and how the design meets it - this isn't optional paperwork but the evidence base for compliance under EN ISO 13849. This documentation also matters practically: it's what a future engineer or auditor needs to verify the safety design remains valid if the cell is later modified.

sections.title: When to Involve Safety Specialists
learningObjectives: Understand the boundary of Systems Engineer competency in safety design
Recognize when formal safety engineering expertise should be brought in
sections.content: This module builds working literacy in safety PLC design principles - enough to collaborate effectively and recognize what's required. For novel or high-risk cell configurations, involving a dedicated functional safety specialist for formal risk assessment and performance level verification is appropriate, rather than relying solely on this curriculum's coverage for genuinely complex safety-critical design.

questions.question: What standard governs the safety design work covered in this module?
questions.feedback: Correct. EN ISO 13849 is the governing standard for machinery and control system safety design.

questions.question: What is a safety-related control function?
options: A part of a control system specifically responsible for preventing or mitigating hazards
Any software feature regardless of purpose
questions.feedback: Correct. Safety-related control functions specifically address hazard prevention or mitigation.

questions.question: What determines the required performance level for a safety function?
options: A risk assessment of the hazard the function addresses
It's the same fixed level for every scenario
questions.feedback: Correct. Performance level requirements scale with assessed risk, per EN ISO 13849.

questions.question: Why does integrating MoRo's safety behavior with a cell's safety PLC require careful design?
options: Integration is automatic and needs no design work
To confirm the combined system genuinely meets its required performance level
It doesn't - any functional connection is sufficient
questions.feedback: Correct. Combined safety systems need deliberate design validation, not just functional connection.

questions.question: When should a dedicated functional safety specialist be involved?
options: For novel or high-risk cell configurations requiring formal risk assessment
Never - this curriculum covers everything needed
questions.feedback: Correct. This module builds working literacy, but complex cases warrant specialist involvement.
